subtitle: Meeting details and hotel reservations for the Network Graphics Working Group

tldr.problem: The Network Graphics Working Group needed to schedule their next meeting and communicate logistics to members.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC announces that the meeting will be held April 16-18, 1972 at The Mitre Corporation in McLean, Virginia, with contact information for Ira Cotton at Mitre and details for hotel reservations at the Tysons Corner Holiday Inn.
tldr.outcome: The meeting location provided access to network graphics equipment including TIP, teletypes, a Datapoint 3300, a 2741, and an Imlac on loan from another organization.

today: RFC 314 is a historical meeting announcement from March 14, 1972. It documents the logistics of an early working group meeting, showing how the ARPANET community coordinated face-to-face gatherings and shared equipment resources.

sections.title: Meeting Scheduled for April 1972
sections.content: The Network Graphics Working Group meeting is scheduled for April 16-18, 1972 at The Mitre Corporation in McLean, Virginia. The meeting will convene at 6 PM on Sunday evening. Mitre has offered facilities for slides and viewgraphs, and will provide special equipment as requested in advance.
sections.eli5: A meeting about computer graphics is set for mid-April at Mitre in Virginia.

sections.title: Contact Information and Accommodations
sections.content: Attendees should contact Ira Cotton at Mitre as soon as possible to confirm attendance. His phone is (703) 893-3500 x2887 and home phone (for emergencies) is (202) 785-1624. Mitre's address is McLean, Virginia, 22101. Hotel rooms have been reserved at the Tysons Corner Holiday Inn, approximately one mile from Mitre on Route 123. Rooms are $19 for a single. The Holiday Inn phone number is (703) 893-2100.
sections.eli5: Call Ira Cotton to say you are coming. Hotel rooms are $19 and close by.

sections.title: Available Equipment at Mitre
sections.content: Mitre provided network equipment for demonstrations: a TIP (Terminal Interface Processor), several teletypes, a Datapoint 3300, a 2741 (a type of terminal), and an Imlac on loan. The location provided good facilities for hands-on demonstration of network graphics work. If sufficient interest arose, a banquet would be arranged at a local inn.
sections.eli5: Mitre has many kinds of terminals and computers set up for the group to use.
